metadata.title: Chinese AI Coding Models: Price, Performance & Harnesses
metadata.dataPolicy: Original figures remain preserved except the explicitly requested GLM Flash refresh. The company overview uses one Flash entry; no larger-model benchmark is attributed to it. Other model snapshots are unchanged.
metadata.evaluationDateNote: Benchmark figures were observed on the snapshot date; evaluation-run dates are not consistently disclosed.
metadata.description: Compare GLM Flash, DeepSeek Flash, MiMo, Qwen, Kimi and MiniMax with GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus. Explore coding evidence, API prices, harnesses and subscriptions.

conclusion.text: For heavy coding, GLM Flash subscriptions and DeepSeek’s fast cached API offer low costs; Sol medium has stronger independent coding results, while MiMo deserves serious consideration among Chinese models.

takeaways.text: Sol medium combines stronger coding scores with lower benchmark task costs than either Flash model. Cheap tokens do not guarantee cheap completed tasks.
DeepSeek leads this group in generation speed; GLM Flash scores higher in AA’s common coding harness.
Harness choice substantially changes results. Kimi’s native CLI performs much better on repository tasks than its generic terminal benchmark suggests.
For heavy autonomous use, subscription reset windows, compaction and recovery matter alongside model quality. A large context window alone does not establish reliability.
MiMo offers strong Chinese API value in this snapshot; Opus leads the common coding benchmark but costs substantially more per attempt.

benchmark.title: AA Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmark.costDefinition: API cost per attempt includes unsuccessful attempts.
benchmark.speedDefinition: Output tokens per second and first-answer delay; delay includes thinking.
benchmark.lcrDefinition: AA-LCR measures long-context reasoning, not overnight autonomous success.

interpretation.text: MiMo and Sol medium occupy the attractive combination of coding success and low benchmark spend. GLM is a competitive budget option. DeepSeek’s clearest advantage is speed and inexpensive cached context. Qwen’s higher coding score does not translate into low task cost in this particular test.

caveats.text: Sol’s official context limit is 1.05 million tokens. Above 272,000 input tokens, input/cache rates double and output rates increase 50% for the entire request. Cache writes cost $2.50/M.
DeepSeek off-peak prices are $0.15 input / $0.60 output / $0.003 cached input per million. Max changes reasoning effort, not the per-token tariff; extra reasoning increases billed output.
MiniMax M3’s listed rates double above 512,000 input tokens. Priority serving costs 1.5× standard. Official passive caching has no additional write fee.
Qwen prices are Singapore/international 0902 rates with implicit caching. Explicit caching lists $2.50/M writes and $0.17/M reads.
Opus cache writes cost $5/M for five minutes or $8/M for one hour. Kimi’s corresponding prices are $3/M and $6/M.
AA’s Opus configuration permits fallback. Treat it as the evaluated configuration, rather than a guaranteed pure-model run.
AA lists GLM cached input at $0.026/M, versus Z.ai’s $0.03/M. Benchmark costs retain AA’s reported snapshot; monthly calculations use official prices.
AA’s MiniMax cache-write entry conflicts with current M3 documentation. The AA benchmark attempt cost is retained unchanged.

repository_agent_note.text: DeepSWE v1.1 solved is repository-coding evidence. Cost and time average across AA’s three coding-agent suites, rather than DeepSWE alone. An equivalent current native-agent row for GLM 5.3 Flash or DeepSeek Flash: Not found; no larger GLM model result is substituted for Flash.

long_task_note.text: No matched independent study was found establishing unattended multi-hour completion rates, recovery reliability or failure frequency for GLM Flash versus DeepSeek Flash in their native harnesses.

official.text: Z.ai’s first-party option is ZCode, described by the vendor as optimized for GLM. Goals supports continuous planning, execution and verification. Claude Code is also an explicitly documented Z.ai integration.

recommendation.text: Your existing Claude Code setup is reasonable, particularly if you already use its workflow. For a fresh setup centered on long autonomous Goals, try ZCode alongside it. No controlled Flash-specific comparison proves one is consistently better.

steps.text: Obtain your Z.ai Coding Plan API key. This configuration applies to a Z.ai Coding Plan account.
Merge the configuration into %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json, preserving existing settings.
Map Haiku, Sonnet and Opus aliases to glm-5.3-flash[1m] and use the one-million-token compaction setting shown.
Start a new Claude Code session, select /effort max, then check /status.

compatibility.text: Map all aliases to Flash. Z.ai’s general example also maps larger model aliases, which can consume approximately three times the plan credits.
Update Claude Code if it rejects the [1m] suffix. GLM supports low/high/max effort; intermediate Claude effort settings are translated.
This is Z.ai-supported compatibility. Anthropic says non-Claude models through gateways are not officially supported by Anthropic. External-key requests do not require a Claude subscription.

There is no automatic API-balance fallback when plan quota runs out. Normal GLM PAYG uses https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4. Anthropic-route PAYG requires a never-subscribed, manually allowlisted account; previously subscribed accounts remain subject to the route restriction.

recommendation.text: Use native Standard mode for working projects. Minimal’s strong vendor benchmark does not establish that it is best for overnight development; the Minimal SDK profile omits several workspace and context-management features.

benchmarkNote.text: These are vendor-run, same-model results, not directly comparable to AA Terminal-Bench 4.0. The headline DeepSWE result uses mini-swe-agent, not the native harness.

setup.text: Use the direct DeepSeek provider. Add your API key under Settings → Models, choose deepseek-flash, and select max effort for difficult work.

limitations.text: The harness is a developer preview, with experimental features and expected breaking changes.

interpretation.text: Strengths: fast generation, inexpensive cached context and good vendor-reported tool use. Limitations: weaker AA common-harness coding results, sensitivity to harness configuration and limited independent evidence for long unattended sessions.

billingNote.text: Individual quarterly and annual prices are paid upfront.

annualConflict.text: Team annual pricing is ambiguous: advertised effective monthly prices are $79.20/$169.20, but public billing data lists initial annual invoices of $1,056/$2,256 and discounted renewals of $950.40/$2,030.40. Team requires at least two seats.

supportedTools.text: Plans support ZCode, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Cline and other documented clients.

rateLimits.text: Z.ai does not publish a fixed RPM/TPM or concurrency guarantee for these tiers; serving limits are dynamic.

creditFormula.text: (uncached input tokens × 2.3 + cached input tokens × 0.56 + output tokens × 8) / 10,000

offpeak.text: Ordinary off-peak usage consumes half the credits.

exhaustion.text: Individual-plan exhaustion does not automatically bill API balance. Team can enable paid overage.

campaign.text: The current half-credit promotion and nighttime Flash campaign end 7 October 2026. The nighttime window is 23:00–09:00 Singapore, or 02:00–12:00 Sydney AEDT. Eligible ZCode/AutoClaw usage consumes no quota; other agents receive increased quota. Conditions include restrictions when existing quotas are exhausted. Temporary offers are excluded from ongoing cost estimates.

billing.text: No verified official flat-fee coding subscription was found. Harness software is free; inference uses prepaid API balance.

rateLimits.text: Flash has an account-level concurrency limit of 2,500. This is not a throughput guarantee.

peakWindows.text: Peak windows are weekdays 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, excluding Chinese public holidays: 12:00–15:00 and 17:00–21:00 Sydney AEDT. Other hours receive the lower tariff.

limits.text: Allowances are normalized and shared, not additive pools or cash API credits. Limits: 20% per five hours, 50% per week and 100% per month.

compatibility.text: Claude Code and ZCode integrations are documented. DeepSeek Harness has a known adapter-header compatibility issue; prefer direct API billing for its native harness. Go uses its own integration configuration; the Z.ai JSON applies to Z.ai accounts.

workload_notes.text: These are transparent planning scenarios, not measured developer averages. Heavy represents aggregate parallel agents; quota eligibility does not guarantee sufficient serving capacity.
The medium scenario fits Lite at off-peak credit rates, but exceeds Lite’s five-hour and weekly allowances if all usage receives peak rates.
Calculations hold token volumes constant. Actual completed-task costs differ because models generate different amounts of reasoning, retry differently and succeed at different rates.

deepseek_offpeak.note: Half peak tariff, with unchanged tokens/cache behavior. Arithmetic estimate, not an off-peak benchmark rerun.

final_recommendations.text: Best balanced primary agent: Sol medium in Codex. It has the strongest combination here of independent repository-coding results, task cost and turnaround time. Use higher effort selectively.

Best budget subscription candidate: GLM Flash in your existing Claude Code workflow. Consider Go Plus for price, or Z.ai Pro for direct vendor service and ZCode access. Choose using measured quota consumption.
Best fast, cached API option: DeepSeek Flash with native Standard Harness. Direct API billing avoids subscription reset windows and the Go compatibility issue. Schedule flexible work off-peak.
Best additional Chinese API trial: MiMo V2.6 Pro. Its common-harness results justify testing it on your repositories before committing to GLM or DeepSeek alone.
Premium escalation option: Opus 5.5. Its stronger common-harness score supports selective use on difficult work; its evaluated max configuration has substantially higher cost and latency.
Use Kimi with its native CLI. Qwen merits consideration within an existing Alibaba workflow. MiniMax would not be the first choice for autonomous coding based on this specific benchmark.

final_note.text: For unattended sessions, the unresolved question is successful completion on your own repositories. Record completed tasks, total spend, elapsed time and required interventions; token price alone will miss the largest differences.

value_zone.rule: Value zone: Intelligence Index ≥40 and illustrative 3:1 uncached blended price ≤$2/M. Among the ten plotted models, the median Intelligence Index is 40.6, so 40 is a simple near-median screening cutoff; $2 is half Sol’s $4/M illustrative blend. These round thresholds are analyst inference and user-adjustable, not a measured benchmark, model ranking or cost per successful task.

multi_model_workflow.title: My multi-model workflow
intro: Tasks are split by difficulty and cost.
The expensive model is used only where strong reasoning is needed.
Token-heavy exploration, file reading and mechanical edits go to cheaper models in the opencode Go subscription, keeping quality high while saving usage quota.

cards.does: Planning, architecture, task breakdown, complex implementation, hard debugging, key decisions and reviews of important subagent output.
cards.why: Strongest reasoning where mistakes cost most; medium/high for daily coding and xhigh reserved for hard problems.

cards.does: Explorer / general subagents: repo search, file reading, code-structure summaries, implementation checks, simple and repetitive edits.
cards.why: Exploration uses the most tokens but needs little reasoning; low cost and a generous quota reduce main-model usage.

cards.does: Medium-difficulty implementation from the lead’s plan: multi-file changes, tests and ordinary bug fixes.
cards.why: More thinking than exploration without using the lead model; max effort compensates for Flash-tier reasoning depth.

cards.does: UI components, styling, layout and interactions.
cards.why: Smaller Go quota: use sparingly, bundle the complete frontend task and hand it over once to avoid back-and-forth.

cards.model_name: Qwen3.8 Flash and MiMo V2.6 Pro

trials.text: Planned trial for parallel exploration, document summaries, batch mechanical edits or a fallback when DeepSeek quota runs low.
Planned trial as a second implementation choice for medium tasks or plan+build, or a fallback when GLM quota runs low.

cards.why: Not enough hands-on test data; compare the same task set before deciding.

flow: After a big chunk of work, review and update project rules

practices.title: Move exploration out of the main model
practices.reason: Exploration is the biggest source of token use, so moving it saves the most.

practices.title: Tell the main agent in AGENTS.md to save tokens and delegate first
practices.reason: This makes the layering happen instead of relying on ad-hoc reminders.

practices.title: Review and add project rules after each big chunk of work
practices.reason: The setup becomes more efficient over time without becoming over-complicated.

validation_plan.title: Validation plan
validation_plan.text: Run the same task set—repo exploration summary, adding a small feature from a plan, batch test writing and fixing a medium bug—2–3 times on each candidate model. Compare quality, speed and quota use, then decide the default split.

multi_model_workflow.footnote: This split is based on task roles and quota considerations, and will be adjusted after hands-on testing.
